A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLPO work, with matching authors, core methodology, and overlapping results. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable throughout. The comparison includes v2's Appendices A–D; the supplied v1 ends with references.

before.justification: v1 reports original search-strategy ablations, human-survey outcomes, concept-similarity measurements, and deletion and fine-tuning analyses in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds feedback comparisons, sentiment-analysis examples, prompt-sensitivity findings, and further model-specific results.

M1.justification: The core DQN, TCAV preference, and Stable Diffusion/LoRA procedure remains. v2 revises the printed reward recurrence and makes scaling concept-specific in Section 3.3, and adds a text variant using Mistral-generated synonyms and TextCNN feedback. Its printed reward update conflicts with Algorithm 2, leaving the implemented schedule unclear.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained ImageNet image-explanation coverage, v2 adds positive and negative text-sentiment explanations using an IMDB-trained TextCNN (Section 4.5 and Appendix D.4). Appendix C.4 also evaluates incoherent seed prompts. The five vision classifiers were already named in v1 and are not newly added coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 adds human-feedback and LLM-feedback variants as comparators to TCAV-feedback RLPO. The EAC, Lens, CRAFT, and epsilon-greedy comparator sets remain. Figure 7 changes the reported comparator from Anchors to LIME while retaining matching visual outputs, so the PDFs do not establish a new baseline execution.

E3.justification: v2 introduces live human/LLM feedback protocols with timing and resource comparisons, plus a text-sentiment evaluation procedure. Retained tables replace CV with inverse CV and accuracy with Exploration Gap, defined as 1 minus accuracy. Survey labels change from n=26/22 to n=260/240, while Appendix D.6 specifies 50 participants answering ten items; the expert-count revision is unexplained and does not establish recollection of data.

E4.justification: v2 adds feedback-source ablations, a failed gibberish-prompt test, training-reward analyses across models, and additional deletion examples. The original unclipped zebra-deletion panel is omitted, while its clipped counterpart remains. The combined-action analysis is retained as Appendix D.3.2 rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Appendix C.1 newly reports run-to-run instability of SGD-based TCAV when explaining the logistic-regression choice. This is limited qualitative information about variability: no run counts, random seeds, or uncertainty estimators are specified. The plus-minus reporting convention already existed in v1; its extension to timing results does not itself establish a new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds feedback execution times of 180±30 seconds for human feedback, 72±1.2 for AI feedback, and 56±0.7 for TCAV feedback, alongside sentiment-word scores and further concept, reward, and deletion results. The embedding-comparison values in v1 Table 3 and v2 Table 4 are unchanged. The transformed survey and search metrics do not demonstrate improved performance.

T1.justification: The three theorem statements from v1 Section 3.5 are retained in Appendix B, but v2 adds substantial proof arguments beyond the earlier sketches. These include a piecewise reward derivation and a concept-set evolution and limiting argument. The new reasoning introduces assumptions, including monotonic TCAV scores, rather than merely changing notation or placement.

C1.justification: The central claims about generating novel, abstract concepts and diagnosing neural networks remain. Introduction contribution 3 newly makes NLP generalizability and actionability through fine-tuning explicit headline contributions, extending the earlier visual diagnostic emphasis.

C2.justification: v2 argues that human/LLM feedback captures semantic relationships without providing model-specific explanations, and its gibberish-prompt findings qualify v1's assertion that seeds do not directly affect accuracy. Existing latency, domain-specificity, and abstraction-control limitations remain. Section 4.4 also introduces an incorrect highest-AUC interpretation that contradicts Figure 8's lower-is-better caption and values.

D1.justification: Appendices C–D supply previously unavailable model checkpoints and TCAV layers, logistic-regression settings, LoRA rank and scaling, DQN hyperparameters, BLIP questions and filtering, image-group sizes, the diffusion preference objective, and fine-tuning and survey procedures. These substantially expand reproducibility information without establishing changes to the previously reported experiments. Some details conflict, including eight feedback participants in Section 4.2 versus seven in Appendix D.2.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly positions the optimization relative to Diffusion-DPO and adds references for human/AI feedback, BLIP, and VLM-based filtering. Appendix A expands discussion of the already-cited EAC and LCDA methods. Robotics-related citations and the Anchors/GradCAM references are removed, while the central generation-versus-retrieval positioning remains.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative through numbered contributions, reordered seed-extraction and RL subsections, and rewritten experimental explanations. Theory, preprocessing details, and combined-action analysis move into organized appendices. Terminology shifts toward seed prompts and preference optimization throughout.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the introductory illustration, adds an explicit RLPO workflow diagram and comparative concept montage, and transposes the dense novelty table into a more readable structure. It also revises the visual explanation comparison, restructures deletion displays, and adds appendix pipelines, concept illustrations, training curves, and survey screenshots. Several existing figures are retained in new locations.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the method easier to inspect and reproduce by supplying previously missing objectives, implementation settings, and study procedures, and adds useful tests of feedback and seed choices. These benefits are tempered by conflicting reward updates, inconsistent participant counts, and the reversed deletion interpretation. The result is a limited net quality gain; the expanded documentation and evidence do not resolve important validation problems.
